acquisition-acquisition:ashbyhq:caf774b2.description: ROLE As the Director of Business Workshops, you'll teach entrepreneurs the Acquisition.com http://Acquisition.com sales and marketing frameworks from the stage and the round-tables, alongside the finance and operations context that makes them work. You'll present to a room full of founders, then go deeper to help them unpack their specific business constraints. The frameworks and the access are already ours; your job is to make them land. The hard part is holding the room, making complex frameworks simple, answering hard questions in real time, and then helping a founder see what they cannot see about their own business. Events run two days: a presentation-heavy first day teaching the full room from the stage, then a more intimate second day going deeper with business owners around the table. Between events, the work is studying, researching incoming cohorts, answering founder follow-ups, running a retrospective on the last event, and continuing to iterate on the format and materials. The stage is the visible part; the preparation and iteration around it are most of the job. You'll present workshops on stage within your first 30 days. We view our Advisory Practice as a professional sport and we welcome your application if you're up for the challenge! RESPONSIBILITIES - Present to founders: teach the Acquisition.com http://Acquisition.com sales and marketing frameworks on stage, with the finance and operations context that makes them work. - Make the frameworks land: translate frameworks into clear lessons that founders can apply immediately, across sales, marketing, finance, and operations. - Diagnose business constraints: go deeper in intimate round-tables and sidebar conversations to help founders identify their core problem. - Study incoming cohorts: between events, research the next group of business owners and prepare rigorously for the room. - Hone your craft: run a retrospective after each event, answer founder follow-ups, and iterate on the format, materials, and presentation. - Strengthen your team: collaborate with peers across the Advisory Practice and ACQ, and help your teammates get better. REQUIREMENTS - Commands a room, large or small. Holds the stage, draws people out at the table, and fields hard questions live. Presence, not rah-rah charisma. - Deep in sales and marketing, fluent enough in finance and operations to read the whole business, and able to make it all simple. - Scaled or exited a business as an operator who owned the P&L, at least seven figures. You diagnose from having carried the number, not just advised on it. - All in and self-directed: fully committed with no outside company, energized by the prep between events as much as the stage. - Relentless about improving the craft, treating every event as a chance to get sharper. - Makes the whole team better, not just yourself, and easy to build with. RESULTS - Founders leave each event able to name the true constraint in their business - Founders experience a moment of clarity that changes how they think about their company and their role as CEO - Both days land: the presentation holds the full room, and the round-tables move each founder forward - Event satisfaction and engagement scores stay high, and founder follow-ups are answered promptly - Each event improves on the last through your retrospectives and iteration - You present on stage within your first 30 days - The advisory team performs better because of your contribution SCHEDULE - Between events, standard business hours spent researching incoming cohorts, answering founder follow-ups, running event retrospectives, and iterating on the material - On the two-day events, expect long days, roughly 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM, plus preparation and debrief around them LOCATION - Las Vegas, NV (onsite) - Relocation support provided; short-term travel during relocation may be acceptable for the first one to two months COMPENSATION - $200,000 to $260,000 base salary plus up to 20 percent annual bonus - The

jobgether-jobgether:lever:61d59478-a555-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Principal Application Security Engineer based in the United States. This is a senior technical leadership role focused on embedding application security into software engineering at enterprise scale. You will partner with development, DevOps, platform engineering, and SRE teams to reduce risk while enabling fast, secure delivery. The role combines hands-on security engineering with strategic influence across applications, APIs, cloud environments, and CI/CD pipelines. You will shape secure-by-design practices, scalable controls, reference architectures, automation, and engineering standards. You will also help advance security approaches for AI-enabled applications and responsible use of AI in software development. Success requires strong technical judgment, credibility with engineers, and the ability to turn complex security risks into practical solutions. This is an opportunity to influence security maturity across a large, distributed engineering organization while remaining close to the technology. Lead complex secure code reviews, threat modeling exercises, and secure design assessments across applications, APIs, and shared services, translating technical findings into actionable guidance. Design, integrate, and continuously improve application security controls across CI/CD platforms, developer workflows, and engineering environments. Identify security control gaps, coverage weaknesses, and delivery friction, then drive remediation through automation, platform improvements, and secure-by-design patterns. Define and promote secure coding standards, reference architectures, playbooks, tooling, and automated security capabilities that can scale across engineering teams. Act as a senior security advisor to engineering and platform teams, influencing architecture, design decisions, remediation strategies, and development practices. Advance application security for AI-enabled development and applications by assessing emerging threats, establishing practical guardrails, and promoting responsible AI adoption. Provide deep expertise in API security, including authentication, authorization, monitoring, secure integration patterns, and protection against common attack techniques. Partner with web and platform teams to design, deploy, and optimize application-layer protections such as WAF policies and rules. Help strengthen software supply chain security through dependency management, pipeline hardening, SBOM practices, artifact integrity, provenance, and package governance. Define application security metrics, maturity indicators, and risk-based reporting to prioritize improvements and demonstrate measurable impact. Requirements: 10+ years of experience in Application Security Engineering, with significant hands-on experience integrating security into software design, development, and delivery. Deep expertise in secure application architecture, secure coding, code-level vulnerability analysis, threat modeling, and application security assessment. Background in software engineering, application development, or architecture, with the ability to operate credibly from high-level design through code and runtime environments. Strong knowledge of authentication, authorization, session management, secrets management, API security, and common vulnerability classes including OWASP Top 10 risks, injection, deserialization, SSRF, insecure design, access-control issues, and dependency vulnerabilities. Hands-on experience securing modern technology stacks such as C#, Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, or comparable languages and frameworks. Strong experience integrating SAST, SCA, DAST, IaC scanning, container security, API security testing, and software supply chain controls into CI/CD pipelines and developer workflows. Proven ability to independently investigate complex technical problems, identify root causes

jobgether-jobgether:lever:e47bad4b-e9bc-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Culinary Operations & Food Systems based in Brazil. This is a senior culinary leadership role focused on building the systems that make food quality, safety, and consistency scalable across multiple locations. You will assess culinary operations, identify urgent product and quality issues, and establish practical standards that can withstand growth and team turnover. The role combines culinary expertise with operational discipline, covering recipes, specifications, food safety, menu performance, training, suppliers, and food economics. Rather than managing daily kitchen execution, you will provide remote leadership through on-site culinary leaders and location teams. You will use data and modern technology to diagnose problems, improve processes, and make informed decisions about products and menus. Success will require balancing exacting culinary standards with commercial realities such as food cost, waste, labor, and margin. This is an opportunity to build durable culinary infrastructure and develop leaders across a distributed operation. Assess the current state of products, menus, recipes, processes, and suppliers using operational data, reports, and remote evidence to identify quality, consistency, and efficiency gaps. Diagnose taste, consistency, product, and food-safety issues and direct corrective actions through on-site Head Chefs and location teams. Develop controlled recipes, specifications, preparation standards, and operating procedures with clear tolerances, documentation, and version control. Lead menu engineering initiatives by analyzing product performance and determining which offerings should be improved, repositioned, or discontinued. Establish robust food-safety, quality assurance, and traceability controls, including root-cause analysis and corrective actions when failures occur. Recruit, train, coach, and develop culinary leaders across multiple locations, creating consistent standards and strengthening leadership capabilities remotely. Establish systems that allow culinary quality to remain consistent despite team turnover, geographic distance, and operational growth. Own the culinary drivers of food cost, yield, waste, labor efficiency, and margin, identifying opportunities to improve commercial performance without compromising quality. Use AI, data, and other technology tools to support culinary analysis, operational decision-making, documentation, training, and continuous improvement. Partner with on-site culinary leadership to translate strategic standards into practical execution and ensure accountability across locations. Requirements Significant senior-level culinary leadership experience within complex, multi-location food service, restaurant, hospitality, or related environments. Demonstrated ability to diagnose product and quality problems, restore consistency, and build repeatable culinary systems rather than relying solely on individual expertise. Experience leading and directing kitchen execution remotely through on-site culinary leaders and distributed teams. Strong understanding of food cost, yield management, waste reduction, labor economics, and the relationship between culinary decisions and profitability. Proven experience with food safety, quality assurance, traceability, and root-cause analysis. Strong practical knowledge of recipe development, food specifications, menu engineering, culinary standards, and process documentation. Advanced, practical use of AI and data tools to support culinary management, operational analysis, and decision-making. Strong leadership and communication skills, with the ability to influence teams and maintain high standards without being physically present.
